meaning: Contracts map host witness needs. They do not certify each consuming application.

identity.contract: Retain resource namespace, operation identity, and exact revision at every codec boundary.
identity.gap: Each application must establish its authoritative namespace and old-format mapping.

files.contract: Separate portable spelling, an admitted root, observed identity, and serialized publication.
files.gap: Per-filesystem path aliases, durability, and external writers need the actual host adapter.

authority.contract: Grant and approval bind the current principal, operation, target, and basis at effect admission.
authority.gap: Candidate Boolean witnesses do not implement real accounts, signing, or workspace trust.

network.contract: A response, readable verified content, and an effect acknowledgement are different observations.
network.gap: Provider authentication, pagination and reconciliation require application protocol evidence.

process.contract: Closing an owning scope requests cancellation and stops admission. Captured resources survive until confirmed retirement or non-execution.
process.gap: Process-tree ownership and detached descendants are platform-specific; candidate process runs are not an all-descendant guarantee.

evidence.contract: Retain observed facts, independent integrity evidence, completeness, and policy decisions separately.
evidence.gap: A digest cannot itself establish publisher identity or undiscovered dependency coverage.

revision.contract: Captured source revision, persisted store revision, document incarnation, and current buffer revision have distinct meanings.
revision.gap: VS Code provider dirty-marker conformance is contradicted in the tested fixture; normal user files remain unqualified.

content.contract: Retain immutable, bounded content before publishing a durable reference, then verify the consumer's actual input evidence.
content.gap: Physical power loss, eviction, and malicious byte substitution need separate recovery/integrity tests.

retention.contract: Saved roots, undo, plans, worker borrowers, recovery and cache owners contribute complete live references reached through retaining edges. Historical/provenance links may legitimately outlive their target content.
retention.gap: The root closure and publication/reclamation coordination must be established for each storage implementation.

concurrency.contract: Check expected revisions in the serialization protocol that applies the effect. Coordinate root publication with reclamation.
concurrency.gap: A metadata transaction alone cannot serialize external asset deletion or uncooperative writers.

ui.contract: Display the saved captured revision and current unsaved work independently. Preserve actual operation outcome and draft.
ui.gap: Dirty marker diverged from disk/buffer state for the provider fixture. Keyboard focus, assistive technologies, and human interpretation remain untested.

publication.contract: Only a committed revision referencing retained content becomes authoritative. A write-request success or uncertain acknowledgement cannot announce completion.
publication.gap: Crash/power-failure behavior and durable backing-store barriers require native failure injection.

capability.contract: Admit the exact requested effect only when the selected host exposes its required capability and permissions.
capability.gap: An API property existing does not establish permission or successful operation; native companions are unimplemented here.

terminal.contract: Observe input and both output streams independently; retain separate bytes, input events, exit, cancellation, and scoped effects.
terminal.gap: PTY attachment does not establish a person or permission to answer. GUI/browser input needs a separate adapter.

archives.contract: Bound actual decompressed reads and establish native confinement independently of entry names and declared sizes.
archives.model: Lifecycle.consume with identity and coverage witnesses
archives.gap: The POSIX probe supports one path component only. Nested archive formats, Windows reparse points, case collisions, and parser equivalence need dedicated checks.

overlay.contract: An effective view retains backing-resource identity and owner. Precedence, enablement, and ordering remain domain policies.
overlay.gap: MO2 VFS, package linker topology, and application config merge order require their own source/native comparisons.

finalization.contract: Accepted writes, completed streams, verified bytes, and acknowledged finalization are distinct phases.
finalization.gap: Native installer completion, distribution upload, and browser external download acceptance are separate consumers.

resources.contract: Resource admission, operation completion, release by each owner, and physical reclamation have different witnesses.
resources.gap: Tracked accounting does not measure total resident memory or driver allocation.

time.contract: Use clocks within named domains and add queueing and admission to any promised bound. A timeout cannot establish rollback.
time.gap: No measured fairness, worst-case latency, or total causal order across independent streams is claimed.
